title: Bound the nicks a client can make the agent keep
description:
`Names` grows without bound from the socket. `Session::who`
(crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/command.rs) returns `Who::User(uri)` for any
syntactically valid `mimi://<domain>/u/<local>` the client types, and WHOIS then
calls `Names::identity`, which mints and keeps a nick through `take_nick`.
Nothing is ever removed from `nicks`, `users` or `when`
(crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs), and docs/design/agent-frontends.md says
"Flood control: none on loopback", so a client can make the daemon hold as many
nicks as it has memory for. Each entry is small, and the connection is the
user's own and authenticated, which is why this is a limit and not a hole.

AGENTS.md: "Every size, depth and count limit is a named constant, enforced at
parse time. Fail closed." There is no constant here.

WHAT NOT TO DO: a bounded mirror of the mapping with an eviction policy, which
decision mimid-1wgh.143 rejected for WHOWAS. Evicting from a copy buys
divergence from the authoritative mapping, and WHOWAS then answers 406 for the
user's own nick while WHOIS still answers for it. Whatever the bound is, it has
to be on the mapping itself, and it has to say what happens to a nick already
shown in a client's scrollback when it is dropped.

A cheaper shape to consider first: mint a nick only for a user the store knows
or that a room names, and answer WHOIS of an invented URI without keeping
anything.
